position_on: the key's own pole: raising the minimum wage and protecting workers, including a $17 minimum wage, expanded overtime pay and a shorter workweek with no loss in pay
confidence_reason: Three of his own Senate releases from 2025 and 2026 call the $7.25 minimum wage a starvation wage that must rise to at least $17, push to expand overtime pay and back a 32-hour workweek with no loss in pay; held at 0.85, the ceiling, because the sources are first-party statements and none is a vote.

sources.excerpt: "The $7.25 an hour minimum wage is a starvation wage. It must be raised to a living wage – at least $17 an hour," ... "In the year 2025, a job should lift you out of poverty, not keep you in it."
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-25 (the release's full text, as published on his Senate site). Release on the Raise the Wage Act he introduced with Rep. Scott. Only the quote attributed to Sanders is used.

sources.excerpt: "We should be making it easier, not harder, for Americans who work more than 40 hours a week to get the time-and-a-half pay that they have earned and deserve. That’s precisely what this bill would do."
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-25 (the release's full text, as published on his Senate site). Release on the Restoring Overtime Pay Act. Only the quote attributed to Sanders is used, not Takano's.

sources.excerpt: "One important way to do that is through a 32-hour workweek with no loss in pay or benefits," ... "A 32-hour workweek is not a radical idea."
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-25 (the release's full text, as published on his Senate site). Release on reintroducing his 32-hour workweek bill. Only the quote attributed to Sanders is used.
